evals.name: sweep-asks-about-security-and-deploy-the-user-never-raised
evals.prompt: we want to build an internal tool for the ops team to approve vendor invoices — a list page with filters, an approve/reject button with a comment box, and an export to Excel at month end. it's bigger than one session so chart it. local markdown is fine. the destination: a written spec the two devs can build from. the things i keep going back and forth on are: whether filters are server-side or client-side, whether the approve button needs a confirm dialog, and what the export columns are.
evals.expected_output: A charting run that grills the user's own three concerns first, then — before the gate — asks ONE batched question naming the areas the user never raised (security, identity/RBAC, data, deploy/rollback, operations, reliability, performance, dependencies, scope) with a recommendation, digs only into the ones the user picks, records every unpicked area as none in a single 'sweep <date>:' notes bullet in the dry run, and does not declare 'no map needed' before the sweep has run.
assertions: Asks about the user's own three concerns (filters, confirm dialog, export columns) before asking about any area the user did not raise
Asks, in ONE batched question, which of the untouched areas matter, and that question names at least security and deploy (rollback) among them
The batched question leads with the agent's own recommendation of which areas matter and waits for the user to answer rather than answering for them
Does not ask ten separate area questions in a row before the user's own concerns have been grilled
Every area the user did not pick appears under 'none' in a single notes line of the form 'sweep <YYYY-MM-DD>: none — …' shown in the dry run
Does not declare that no map is needed before the sweep has been run
Runs the dry run and asks for a yes before writing anything with --real

evals.name: charted-from-a-briefing-every-question-opens-with-the-frame-line
evals.prompt: chart a map for ADO Feature #193 (children #194-#197), stage plan (2/4), local markdown, folder ado-193-ips-api-feed. The briefing's open points, each with its letter and locator: A · #195 AC-1 · NAT gateway shape - SKU, IP, subnets and names? · not named; B · #195 AC-2 · IPS password - by which safe route does it reach Key Vault? · Scott van der Kreek; C · #196 AC-4 · Retries - how does the sync handle a transient network or API error? · not named. Group 1: B. Group 2: A, C. B blocks C. Destination to confirm with me: every question that blocks building #195 and #196 has a recorded answer.
evals.expected_output: A charting run whose every message to the person opens with the Frame line: the destination question '#193 · briefing · chart map ado-193-ips-api-feed · question 1 of 4 · plan (2/4)', then one question per point opening with that point's letter and locator, then the sweep question, then the gate.
assertions: The destination question opens with '#193 · briefing · chart map ado-193-ips-api-feed · question 1 of 4 · plan (2/4)'; a backend ask before it opens with '#193 · backend · chart map ado-193-ips-api-feed · plan (2/4)'
The question about point C opens with '#196 AC-4 · briefing point C · chart map ado-193-ips-api-feed · question 4 of 4 · plan (2/4)' or the same line with its own position in the count
The sweep's one batched question opens with '#193 · sweep · chart map ado-193-ips-api-feed · question 5 of 5 · plan (2/4)' (the count grows by one for the sweep)
The dry-run gate message opens with '#193 · gate · chart map ado-193-ips-api-feed · plan (2/4)'
Every created ticket's Question still ends with a sentence that starts 'Touches' and names the point's locator, e.g. 'Touches #196 AC-4.'
No message to the person opens with a heading, a table or prose before the Frame line
